A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WorldTest and AutumnBench. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 517 human participants and reasoning models, exploration-trajectory analyses, and random-agent simulations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and additionally reports simulator-agent results, prompt-sensitivity experiments, and perplexity–performance correlations.

M1.justification: The proposed WorldTest interaction/test procedure, challenge transformations, and AutumnBench task mechanisms remain unchanged. The new Autumn-simulator agent is an additional comparison baseline, rather than a replacement or component change to the proposed framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 43 grid-world environments, 129 masked-frame prediction, change-detection, and planning tasks, and 517 human participants. The new prompt experiment uses existing environments; no additional domain or task family is evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 adds a ground-truth Autumn-simulator comparator in Figure 3 and Appendix E.2.1. Gemini 2.5 Flash and Qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507, already present in v1's cost analysis, also enter the broader task, environment, and behavioral comparisons. The random baseline is retained, not newly introduced.

E3.justification: v3 adds a four-prompt comparison covering all three tasks from eight existing environments, and a simulator evaluation with planning search depth and breadth capped at 10. The original human aggregation, task scoring, interfaces, and single-trajectory reasoning-model evaluation remain specified as before.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.3.2 tests sensitivity to explicit instructions, an automatically refined prompt, and human-tutorial examples. Appendix E.4.2 tests whether perplexity predicts success using pooled and within-agent correlations. These address questions untested in v1; the existing cost analysis and 6JVMF reasoning trace are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces Pearson/Spearman correlation tests with p-values and sample counts, plus mean-plus/minus reporting for prompt comparisons, whose dispersion measure is unspecified. It also reports 10,000 repetitions for simulator procedures. The original 20 human attempts per problem and single-trajectory reasoning-model evaluation are unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds simulator, prompt-comparison, correlation, and expanded model-result entries. Existing scores also change: between v1 Table E.1 and v3 Table E.2, Gemini 2.5 Pro on KFQYT changes from 0 to 1 for masked-frame prediction and from 1 to 0 for planning; human DQ8GC masked-frame prediction changes from 1 to 0. These revisions are not accompanied by documented setting changes.

T1.justification: New Appendix E.1 supplements the retained framework with a next-state-model formulation, including a masked-frame posterior and Monte Carlo estimator and an entropy-scaled change-detection threshold. WorldTest's policy codomain is also corrected from the base action space A to the challenge action space A'. Existing task and perplexity definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract's benchmark contribution, human advantage, and mixed compute-scaling findings remain unchanged. v3 refocuses the introduction and conclusion on environment-level queries and explicitly claims that some such queries were impossible under RL-based benchmarks. The conclusion expands its empirical headline from three to five reasoning models.

C2.justification: Where v1 mainly interprets lower perplexity as better world-model learning, v3 adds that perplexity weakly predicts success and has no significant within-agent correlations. It discusses hypothesis diversity and human ceiling effects, attributes simulator shortcomings to stochastic inference and planning, and interprets prompt results as primarily reflecting model capabilities. These qualifications are not fully integrated into the main-text interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 documents the simulator's task-specific solvers and search limits, identifies the prompt-test environments and prompt-construction approaches, and adds a dataset-release reference said to contain alternative prompts and complete interaction logs. Existing interface descriptions, original prompt listings, and benchmark-access statements are largely retained.

R1.justification: Beyond moving related work into Section 2, v3 substantially reframes the benchmark taxonomy around environment-level queries. It replaces the earlier white-box critique with output-format and proxy limitations and adds stronger arguments about structural queries excluded by RL evaluation. It also connects the simulator to Dreamer-v3, adding Hafner et al. and removing the Sutton–Barto reference.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work receives its own section, and Appendix E is reorganized into structured theoretical, baseline, performance, behavioral, and qualitative subsections. A duplicated reasoning-model setup paragraph is removed, with terminology and language edits throughout.

P2.justification: v3 combines v1 Figure 4 and Figure 6's score panel into Figure 3, expands comparison plots, and adds axis labels. Score/action tables gain model columns and rotated headers; new tables display prompt and correlation analyses. Figure 6 retains an outdated four-panel caption despite now containing three panels.

improvement.justification: The simulator reference, prompt controls, and direct examination of the perplexity proxy make v3's evaluation more informative and scrutinizable than v1's. Added implementation and release information also helps reproducibility. The overall gain is limited by unexplained revisions to retained scores, incomplete reconciliation of the new perplexity qualifications with the main discussion, and stale figure captions.
